questions.question: 1. Which of the following is an example of an impulse turbine?

explanations.a: Incorrect. Francis turbine is a reaction turbine.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Kaplan turbine operates on the reaction principle.
explanations.c: Correct. Pelton wheel is an impulse turbine in which the entire available head is converted into kinetic energy before striking the buckets.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Propeller turbine is a reaction turbine.

questions.question: 2. In which type of turbine does water flow over the runner at atmospheric pressure?

explanations.a: Correct. In an impulse turbine, the pressure remains atmospheric while passing over the runner.
explanations.b: Incorrect. In reaction turbines, pressure changes occur across the runner.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Mixed-flow turbines are a type of reaction turbine.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Axial-flow turbines operate on the reaction principle.

explanations.b: Correct. Hydraulic turbines convert the energy possessed by water into mechanical energy.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Thermal energy conversion is not the function of hydraulic turbines.

questions.question: 4. Which component of a Pelton wheel turbine directs the jet onto the buckets?

explanations.a: Incorrect. Draft tubes are used in reaction turbines.
explanations.b: Incorrect. The runner receives the jet but does not direct it.
explanations.c: Incorrect. The casing mainly prevents splashing and guides discharged water.
explanations.d: Correct. The nozzle converts pressure energy into kinetic energy and directs the jet onto the buckets.

questions.question: 5. Which turbine is most suitable for low-head and high-discharge conditions?

explanations.a: Incorrect. Pelton turbines are used for high-head applications.
explanations.b: Correct. Kaplan turbines are axial-flow reaction turbines suitable for low-head, high-discharge conditions.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Turgo turbines are impulse turbines for medium heads.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Cross-flow turbines are not preferred for very high discharges.

questions.question: 6. The draft tube in a reaction turbine is used to:

answers.b: Convert pressure energy into electrical energy
answers.c: Recover kinetic energy at the runner exit
answers.d: Increase the head at the inlet

explanations.a: Incorrect. Increasing discharge alone is not the purpose of the draft tube.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Electrical energy conversion occurs in the generator.
explanations.c: Correct. A draft tube helps recover kinetic energy leaving the runner and improves efficiency.
explanations.d: Incorrect. It does not increase the inlet head.

questions.question: 7. The specific speed of a turbine is defined as the speed of a geometrically similar turbine that develops unit power under:

explanations.a: Correct. Specific speed is defined for a turbine producing unit power under unit head.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Specific speed is not based on unit discharge.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Efficiency does not appear in the definition.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Unit velocity is not involved in defining specific speed.

questions.question: 8. Which turbine generally possesses the highest specific speed?

explanations.a: Incorrect. Pelton turbines have comparatively low specific speed.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Francis turbines have moderate specific speed.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Turgo turbines do not possess the highest specific speed.
explanations.d: Correct. Kaplan turbines are characterized by high specific speed and are suitable for low-head applications.

questions.question: 9. Cavitation in hydraulic turbines occurs when:

answers.c: Pressure falls below vapor pressure of water

explanations.a: Incorrect. High pressure does not cause cavitation.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Zero velocity does not initiate cavitation.
explanations.c: Correct. Cavitation occurs when the local pressure drops below the vapor pressure, forming vapor bubbles.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Constant temperature is unrelated to cavitation.
